subject: art-and-design
topicName: Photography and Digital Art in Fine Art

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Photography in fine art uses the camera as a creative tool, not just to document — consider composition, lighting, viewpoint intentionally.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Digital manipulation (Photoshop, apps) can transform images — but ethical considerations matter: how much manipulation is appropriate?

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Moving image (film, animation, video art) adds time and narrative to visual art — consider sequence, pace, sound.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Combining traditional and digital processes creates unique hybrid works.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring photography and digital art in fine art. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with photography and digital art in fine art. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with photography and digital art in fine art. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to photography and digital art in fine art, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to  | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
